thread:
alex: Quick thread  UX review: streaming token display + small edit flow when prompt drawer is open. Thinking of two options: collapsed token badge + inline micro-toolbar, or full floating toolbar that appears above the message while streaming. Which feels less disruptive?
tara: Inline micro-toolbar wins for speed. Floating toolbar overlaps content and on small screens its a mess. Keep controls minimal: stop, regenerate, copy. :zap:
ishaan: Accessibility note: floating widgets often cause focus traps. If we use a floating toolbar make sure its reachable via a single Tab and has aria-modal=false. Also announce \"response streaming\" via a live region when the stream starts.
kelly: Mobile constraints matter: inline toolbar can push the composer up and hide the keyboard. For mobile, prefer a persistent little control in the composer footer that toggles between Stop / Regenerate when applicable. Desktop gets micro-toolbar on hover/focus.
ben: Token counter placement: right now its inside the streaming overlay which VoiceOver reads inconsistently. Proposal: token counter should live in a stable DOM location (composer header) and expose updates through aria-live=\"polite\". Visual updates can be batched.
tara: On the copy front, short labels are important. Use \"Stop\" not \"Cancel\"; \"Regenerate\" vs \"Retry\" we favor \"Regenerate\" for clarity. For tooltip help use sentence-case: \"Stop the response\" vs \"Stop Response\".
ishaan: Performance: avoid updating token DOM every token. Use a 150-250ms render throttle; keep exact counts in telemetry. Also avoid layout shifts by reserving space for the badge (width: min-content with ellipsis fallback).
kelly: Prompt drawer conflict: when the prompt library slides over the right rail it currently hides the token badge. Two options: (1) token badge floats above drawer with a subtle shadow, (2) token badge collapses into a small icon in the header that opens a mini panel. Which do we prefer?
alex: Leaning to (2) because floating over the drawer feels hacky and can cause hit-target overlap. Collapsing into header icon keeps a single stable place for token info. We should animate the collapse so users notice the change.
ben: Visual affordance idea: show a thin animated underline on the last streaming token to indicate playback. If user presses Stop it becomes a static end-marker. Might help users understand progression.
tara: A11y nit: color contrast on the token badge in our current dark theme is marginal at small sizes. Increase contrast or add a 1px border. Also provide a text-only mode for high-contrast accessibility setting.
ishaan: Keyboard mapping: Ctrl+\\. to stop stream (non-conflicting), Ctrl+Shift+R to regenerate. Make sure those shortcuts are discoverable in the keyboard help overlay. After stop, focus returns to generated message; if user invoked Stop with a shortcut, focus should go to the stop control briefly then back to content.
kelly: Edge-case: long prompts + streaming + prompt drawer open can cause memory spikes due to repeated DOM diffs. Suggest we only mount streaming DOM for visible viewport messages and use virtualization for older messages.
alex: Action items:
- tara -> mocks for desktop micro-toolbar + header-collapsed token icon (due Wed)
- ishaan -> live-region + keyboard shortcut spec, and a11y acceptance tests
- kelly -> mobile composer footer controls prototype + perf notes
- ben -> animation spec for token underline + small copy doc
I'll create a short checklist entry for PRs: token badge accessibility, focus preservation, debounce setting.
alex: Thanks all. Can we aim to ship the UX experiment behind a feature flag and watch engagement? Drop any follow-ups in #design-review. :white_check_mark:
